newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures pare gains on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures pare gains on profit-taking.

text.p: The key March Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended Wednesday's Tokyo session higher but well off its intraday high.
The March closed up 0.08 at 126.30 after rising as high as 126.68. Turnover was 48,573 contracts.
Buying was triggered in the morning by rumours, later denied, that Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) might hold an emergency news briefing, traders said.
An NCB spokesman quoted the bank's senior managing director as saying that this rumour, and another that it would be involved in a merger, were groundless.
The Nikkei average of 225 leading shares ended down 128.36 points, or 0.70 percent, at 18,185.97, after falling as low as 17,901.48.
"Some bond dealers took profit in the afternoon after seeing Tokyo stocks pare losses," a brokerage house trader said.
In the cash market, some profit-taking was detected at the long-end of the yield curve, traders said.
The yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB stood at 2.390 percent as of 3.45 p.m. (0645 GMT), unchanged from Tuesday. It had fallen as low as 3.350 percent.
Traders were sceptical about the prospects of the March futures contract rising above its all-time high of 126.83 in the immediate future.
"Vague talks about bank sector problems may not be enough to encourage further upside tests," the brokerage trader said.
Market participants were also cautious about how the dollar/yen would move after the weekend G7 meeting, traders said.
"People are not terribly worried about yen weakness for now. If the exchange rate stabilises after the G7, it would be positive for JGBs," a city bank trader said.
Traders said that as the March JGB futures contract was likely to yield its benchmark status to the June contract later this month, short-covering pressure was expected to limit its downside.
